name: Supporting Teachers of English Learners
title: Supporting Teachers of English Learners
answer: Supporting teachers of English learners means giving non-specialist teachers practical AI help to create sentence frames, glossaries, and simplified texts, while an English language development specialist reviews the work. It matters because most English learners spend most of their day with teachers who are not language specialists, and those teachers need usable supports. The specialist's expertise remains essential, and districts should protect their time for coaching and direct work with students.

sections.body: This idea addresses the gap between the language support English learners need and the preparation most of their teachers have. Most English learners are in general education classrooms for most of the day, so their teachers are usually not language specialists. AI can help those teachers draft materials such as sentence frames, glossaries, and simplified texts for a unit. A language development specialist then reviews those drafts, which keeps quality high. Over time, teachers can build a reusable library of supports.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: In practice, a teacher might ask AI to draft supports for a specific unit and then send them to the English language development specialist for review. Professional learning should show teachers how to prompt for a text at a particular level, how to check a translation, and why AI feedback on student writing needs human review. The supplied text does not give grade bands, so the approach is described generally rather than by grade level. Specialists can also use AI to produce materials faster and share them across schools. Districts should protect specialists' time so they can coach teachers and work with students, not only produce materials.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The text gives no study, figure, or evidence label for this idea. It rests on practice rather than research. The claims are practical: teachers need help, AI can provide some of it, and specialist review is what makes the materials good.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: AI does not replace the expertise of English language development specialists, and that expertise is what makes the materials good. Teachers should understand the tools' limits, including that AI feedback on learners' writing needs review and that translations need checking. The decisions about what students receive and how materials are used stay with educators, especially the specialist who reviews the work. Districts should also protect specialists' time for coaching teachers and working with students, not just for producing materials. The text does not set out legal rules, and this description is about practice.
